description.narrative: The grant has the objective to build a cohesive campaign and amplify the voice of CSOs, communities and workers to realise just transition through ending fossil fuels and upholding human rights. Activity packages- Organise at least 300 groups to carry out 300 physical mobilisation actions in 60countries,- Support grassroot movements and groups with small grants through regional anchors to take simultaneous, symbolic coordinated and strategic actions across world- Support coordinated communication of the mobilisation efforts both online and offline and offer comms support in designs, graphic, etc to the groups organising. Description of the activities:The Global Week of Action (15-21 September) will focus on a broad range of events and actions, both online and in-person, with an emphasis on communications and knowledge-sharing. The Global Days of Action (19-21 September) will feature a combination of large-scale demonstrations and decentralized actions, with an emphasis on rallying in-person people power. We are going to mobilize more than300 groups and movements to carry out300 actions in 60 countries globally. These actions will be supported and coordinated by our allies' regional anchors in Africa, Europe, Asia, Latin America, Pacific Islands, US and UK. Through our regional anchors and allies a small grants will be made available to grassroot groups and movement to take simultaneous and coordinated actions:Mass Rallies <(>&<)> Marches● Coordinated and distributed actions in all regions and major cities worldwide,demonstrating collective power.● Large “lines” (long-distance banners) carried by marchers. Community-Led Actions● Actions at renewable energy or fossil fuel sites, demanding ending of fossil fuels,funding for energy transition and workers rights.● Actions at sites connected with global mining, including banks that enable and profiteer from socio-ecological disaster, demanding divestment from war and a just transition for mining andarms workers.● Human chains to physically "draw the line" between the problem and the solutions. Strikes, Walkouts <(>&<)> Solidarity Actions● By workers and social movements, amplifying the message of economic justice and its intersections with social and climate justice. Teach-outs, Webinars and Workshops● Researchers, organisers and affected communities host different kinds of knowledge-sharing or skill-sharing sessions, online and in-person, to share knowledge and experiences drawing the line for social, climate, economic and racialjustice.● Workshops or meetings to better understand workers’ and their communities’ ideas and plans for just transition. Communications Actions● Media engagement, social media campaigns and other digital actions

participating-org.narrative:
Climate Action Network (CAN) is a global network of more than 1,900 civil society organisations in over 130 countries driving collective and sustainable action to fight the climate crisis and to achieve social justice. CAN convenes and coordinates civil society at the UN climate talks and other international fora.
Since its inception in the 1980s, CAN has grown into a strong, member-driven network with a membership spanning all six continents in over 130 countries.
With its diversity of membership and long-standing experience in steering the climate movement, CAN continues to seek alignment and build bridges with partners and stakeholders across theclimate movement and beyond to pressure governments to take bold and urgent climate action to end the era of fossil fuels and address the needs of the most vulnerable people impacted by the climate crisis.
Climate Action Network International functions as the Secretariat of the network and is independent legally and financially from any members and CAN nodes.
